title: Quantitative Immunoblot Analysis of LRRK1 Signalling Pathway
author: Asad Malik
materials: Immediately transfer the cell dishes to ice.
Scrape the cells on the dish using a cell lifter (Sigma-Aldrich CLS3008, or equivalent) to ensure all cells are detached from the dish.
After incubation with primary antibodies, wash membranes in TBS-T on a see-saw rocker (3 washes, 5-10 minutes per wash).

Analyse immunoblotting data using a software for statistical analysis (Graphpad Prism, or equivalent). Figure 2. Representative results of quantitative immunoblotting analysis of pSer72 Rab7A/total Rab7A and total LRRK1 levels performed in extracts from wild-type (WT) and homozygous LRRK1 knock-out (KO) mouse embryonic fibroblasts treated +/- PKC activator PMA (100 ng/ml, 30 min) according to the protocol described here.

steps.title: Activate LRRK1 in cells
steps.instruction: Treat cells for at least 30 minutes with PMA (a PKC activator) at a final concentration of 100 ng/mL (or equivalent volume of DMSO) before lysis.

steps.title: Prepare cells for lysis
steps.instruction: Rinse cells in the tissue culture dish by carefully pouring room temperature culture media without Foetal bovine serum (FBS) into the dish, then pour off and completely aspirate any residual media.

steps.title: Lyse cells
steps.instruction: Immediately add freshly prepared ice-cold lysis buffer to cover the entire surface. For non-adherent cells, follow a specific pelleting procedure.

substeps.instruction: For adherent cells: Use 0.1-0.2 mL lysis buffer per well of a 6-well plate, 0.5 mL for a 10-cm dish, or 1 mL for a 15-cm dish.

For non-adherent cells: Transfer cells to a Falcon tube, pellet by centrifugation at 180 x g for 3 minutes, wash once with room temperature culture media without FBS, pellet again, discard supernatant, and add ice-cold lysis buffer.
Transfer cell lysate to an Eppendorf tube on ice.

steps.title: Incubate and clarify lysates
steps.instruction: Allow lysates to incubate on ice for 20 minutes for efficient lysis, then clarify by centrifugation.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge at 20,800 x g for 10 minutes at 4 °C.
Transfer supernatants into new Eppendorf tubes and discard the pellet.
Keep tubes on ice (or snap freeze in liquid nitrogen and store at -80 °C).

steps.title: Determine protein concentration
steps.instruction: Measure protein concentration of lysates using a Bradford assay in triplicate according to manufacturer's instructions.

substeps.instruction: Ensure samples are in the linear range; prepare dilutions in water if necessary.
Expected ranges: 0.5 to 5 mg/ml for near confluent cells; at least 2 mg/ml for tissues.

steps.title: Prepare samples for immunoblotting
steps.instruction: Normalize all samples to the same protein concentration (ideally 0.5 µg/µL to 2 µg/µL) by combining lysate with lysis buffer, then add loading buffer.

substeps.instruction: Add 4X SDS/LDS loading buffer freshly supplemented with beta-mercaptoethanol at a 1:4 ratio (e.g., 2.5 µL buffer for 7.5 µL lysate/lysis buffer mix).
Mix by vortexing.
Incubate samples for 5 minutes at 70 °C in a heating block.

steps.title: Load and electrophorese samples
steps.instruction: Load samples and molecular weight markers (10 kDa to 250 kDa) onto a NuPAGE 4–12% Bis–Tris Midi Gel (ThermoFisherScientific, Cat#WG1402BOX or Cat#WG1403BOX) or a self-cast 10% Bis-Tris gel.

substeps.instruction: Rinse wells with running buffer before loading.
Load 10-40 µg of protein per sample: 10-15 µg for MEFs, A549, or human peripheral blood cells; 30-40 µg for mouse brain, spleen, kidney, lung, and intestine.
Include an internal loading control if using multiple gels.
Electrophorese at 130V with MOPS SDS running buffer for 2 hours or until the blue dye runs off the gel.

steps.title: Assemble transfer stack
steps.instruction: Pre-soak the gel, one nitrocellulose membrane (GE Healthcare, Amersham Protran Supported 0.45 μm NC), and two pieces of filter paper (Whatman 3MM Chr Chromatography Paper) in transfer buffer.

substeps.instruction: In a tray of transfer buffer, assemble the stack in a cassette holder in this order: sponge pad (cathode side), filter paper, gel, nitrocellulose membrane, filter paper, sponge pad.
Use a roller to remove air bubbles between layers.
Close the cassette holder and insert it into the transfer tank filled with transfer buffer.

steps.title: Transfer proteins to membrane
steps.instruction: Perform a wet transfer of proteins from the gel to the nitrocellulose membrane at 100 V (constant voltage) for 1.5 hours on ice.

steps.title: Assess transfer and section membrane
steps.instruction: Stain membranes with Ponceau solution to assess efficiency and quality. Divide the membrane into three sections using horizontal cuts based on ladder bands.

substeps.instruction: Top section (above 75 kDa): probe for LRRK1.
Middle section (between 75 kDa and 37.5 kDa): probe for GAPDH/tubulin.
Bottom section (below 37.5 kDa): probe for pS72-Rab7A/Rab7A.
Note: If using anti-phospho(Ser)-PKC Substrates, blot the entire membrane.

steps.title: Block and incubate with primary antibodies
steps.instruction: Destain membranes with TBS-T and block, then incubate with primary antibodies overnight.

substeps.instruction: Incubate in blocking solution for at least 15 minutes at room temperature on a see-saw rocker.
Rinse in TBS-T.

Incubate overnight at 4 °C with primary antibodies diluted in 5% (w/v) BSA in TBS-T (pS72 Rab7A: 1 mg/ml; Rab7A Total: 1 mg/ml; pT202/Y204 ERK1/2: 1 mg/ml; Phospho-(Ser) PKC Substrate: 1 mg/ml; LRRK1 total: 1 mg/ml; GAPDH: 1:5,000; alpha-tubulin: 1:5,000).

steps.title: Incubate with secondary antibodies
steps.instruction: Incubate membranes with near-infrared fluorescent dye-labelled secondary antibodies (diluted 1:20,000) for 1 hour at room temperature on a see-saw rocker.

substeps.instruction: For multiplexing, use spectrally distinct dyes (e.g., IRDye 800CW for phospho-antibodies and IRDye 680LT for total antibodies).
Secondary options include goat anti-mouse (680LT/800CW), goat anti-rabbit (800CW), donkey anti-mouse (680LT/800CW), donkey anti-rabbit (800CW), or donkey anti-goat (800CW for Sheep primary).

steps.title: Wash and image membranes
steps.instruction: Wash membranes and acquire protein bands using infrared detection.

substeps.instruction: Wash extensively in TBS-T on a see-saw rocker (4 washes, 10-15 minutes per wash).
Acquire bands via Odyssey CLx Imaging System and quantify signal using Image Studio Software.
Normalize signal intensity against control samples to account for inter-gel variability.
